Hi.

1. We had a Bunker in our game yesterday who was in Utility mode.

According to the text, it says that while in this mode, he's not allowed to take the Attack or Hinder action. So the PC in our game decided instead to bring down a pile of rubble on the spider bots.

Since this is an indirect attack, does it:

a) count as an attack regardless?

b) count as an Overcome action?

If a), would it mean that Bunker in Utility mode is therefore not allowed to do so?

If b), does it mean it's a Risky Action, as hinted on page 8 of the Starter rules? "An Overcome action also uses the Min die to deal damage to a target in the way."

2. I see folks here mentioning Defending as a Reaction (Hit the Deck) and all other Reactions use only one die. But I can't find this anywhere in the Starter rules. Anyway, for Defending as a Reaction, can the player choose whichever die is the biggest among Power, Quality and Status?

posts.name: catDreaming
posts.cooked:
1.a. That seems like it would count as an Attack action. Ergo, Bunker in utility mode cannot do so.
1.b. If it is taken as a Risky action, then it would still not work. There needs to be some type of Challenge in the scene for Bunker to Overcome. If he can come up with something in the narrative, great. Otherwise, it still would not work. He also would not be using the ability from Utility Mode in that case; It would be an Overcome with Mid die, damage with Min die, and then whatever the Minor Twist he takes is.
2. The player can choose any Power or Quality die, but what they use must be reflected in the narrative for how they are defending against the Attack. Keep in mind that when a player uses Hit The Deck, they also take a Minor Twist immediately afterward, regardless of the results.

1.  That would be an attack and not an option for Bunker in that mode.   Overcomes in general won't cause any damage.

A Challenge in the Sentinel Comics RPG is only solvable using Overcome actions. Minions and Lieutenants have dice sizes, and need to be handled via Attacks unless that particular minion or lieutenant is explicitly stated to be affected by a particular Overcome action.

Generically, letting a Modular character ignore the restrictions on their Modes kind of ruins the point of the archetype.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
The five basic action types are actually effects, not really actions.  Bunker can absolutely bring down the ceiling no matter what mode he's in, but what he can do with it is restricted.

  • Attack: Crush and damage the enemies.
  • Hinder: Trap or otherwise impede the enemies.
  • Boost: Clear a path to make an action easier for an ally.
  • Defend: Create a barrier in between enemies and allies.
  • Overcome: Hard to create a blanket case, because Overcomes are usually done to beat a specific challenge or remove a (named) mod.  But clearly there are situations where it could work.  But an Overcome isn't going to deal damage or create a mod.

Some bots sought out high ground in and all around the park (building facade, park walls, on statues, etc.). They then created thick, protective web cocoons, reconfiguring themselves into fixed laser batteries.

Of course the point of Modular is that you give up some options to be better at others

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked: It's situational, but I'd allow folks to use an overcome to close off an enemy (but the enemy might now be doing something else you don't know about), disable an enemy (as Sea-Envy noted has been done before), or otherwise get around any enemy's threat (e.g., shut down a power source). For example, a player in a demo game of the starter set decide to tie down a spider-bot and disable it (as they wanted to capture it for examination) instead of directly attacking it, and we used an overcome to represent that.
